newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate jumps to 13.4 pct from 11.7.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate jumps to 13.4 pct from 11.7.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate jumped to 13.4 percent on Friday from 11.7, boosted by a larger volume of term loans, dealers said.
They put the daily trading at 38.5 million kuna, which left a surplus of 21.5 million kuna on the supply side.
Fresh borrowings accounted for 11.5 million kuna.
Term loan rates ranged from 13 percent for one-week to 15 percent for one-month loans. Call money was granted at steady 10.5 percent.
Banks renewed 21.2 million kuna loans, with rates ranging from 13 percent for two-week to 19 percent for two-month borrowings.
Insurers charged a steady nine percent for old money.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Saturday and Monday weaker at 5.9913 against the dollar and at 3.5750 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
